items.title: Take-Two: Rockstar has completed development of GTA VI
items.summary: On Take-Two's November 9 earnings call, CEO Strauss Zelnick said Rockstar has finished developing GTA VI and that pre-orders are tracking far above expectations. No pre-order numbers were given.
items.body: "Right now, Rockstar has completed the development of GTA VI," Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said on the company's November 9 earnings call. Take-Two says pre-orders are "continuing to reach unprecedented levels" and are tracking far in excess of its initial expectations, but it didn't share a figure. The launch stays November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

items.title: GTA VI pre-load starts November 10, needs up to 212 GB
items.summary: Rockstar and PlayStation moved digital pre-load to November 10. PS5 starts at local midnight; Xbox Series X|S at 12 a.m. GMT. Clear up to 212 GB. Code-in-box editions arrive November 12.
items.body: Rockstar Games announced that Grand Theft Auto VI digital pre-loading begins on November 10, two days earlier than the previously reported November 12 window. PlayStation 5 downloads open at midnight local time; Xbox Series X|S opens globally at 12 a.m. GMT. Rockstar says the pre-load file needs up to 212 GB depending on the device, matching PlayStation's guidance to reserve 212 GB on PS5.

items.title: Early report put GTA VI at about 210 GB on PS5
items.summary: PlayStation Store data tracker PlayStation Game Size first reported about 210 GB for the Standard Edition on PS5. Rockstar has since confirmed pre-load starts November 10 and needs up to 212 GB.
items.body: According to PlayStation Game Size, which tracks PlayStation Store data, Grand Theft Auto VI's Standard Edition ($79.99) was listed at about 210 GB of storage on PS5. Rockstar Games later confirmed that digital pre-loading begins on November 10, not November 12 as first reported, and that the pre-load needs up to 212 GB depending on the device. The game launches on November 19.

items.title: GTA VI's roads are significantly narrower than GTA V's
items.summary: Rockstar's Aaron Garbut says GTA VI's roads were made much narrower on purpose, for denser traffic and more buildings.
items.body: Rockstar's Aaron Garbut told Bloomberg's Jason Schreier that the roads in Grand Theft Auto VI were deliberately made much narrower than in GTA V. According to Garbut, this leads to denser traffic and leaves more space for buildings to fill the world.

items.title: GTA VI digital pre-orders pass 6.45 million
items.summary: Sensor Tower estimates 6.45 million digital pre-orders worth about $630 million as of October 18, with 74% on PlayStation. Rockstar and Take-Two haven't confirmed any figures.
items.body: Market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimates that Grand Theft Auto VI has reached about 6.45 million digital pre-orders as of October 18, worth roughly $630 million. According to the estimate, 74% of these pre-orders were made on PlayStation. Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive have not confirmed any pre-order figures.

items.title: Rockstar spent years trying to replace the weapon wheel
items.summary: Bloomberg's Jason Schreier says Rockstar tested trays, webs and other layouts for GTA VI's limited, Red Dead-style loadouts before going back to a classic weapon wheel.
items.body: According to Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier, Rockstar spent a long time testing alternatives to the weapon wheel for Grand Theft Auto VI. The experiments, including trays, webs and other layouts, were meant to support more limited, Red Dead-style loadouts. Rockstar reportedly returned to a classic weapon wheel in the end.

items.title: GTA VI Launch Trailer is out
items.summary: Rockstar released the official Launch Trailer, featuring "Flower in a Hurricane". Release stays November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
items.body: Rockstar Games has released the official Launch Trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI. It debuts "Flower in a Hurricane" by Justice feat. Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, from the game's original score. The release date stays November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

items.title: Bloomberg goes inside the making of GTA VI
items.summary: In a Bloomberg Businessweek cover story, Rockstar's leads talk about the two delays and the 2022 leak, and say the next game won't take another eight years.
items.body: Rockstar has grown from 2,441 people in 2018 to 4,711 across 12 studios, according to the report. Studio lead Phil Hooker says "the game is never completely settled" and that the new engine, tools and team should make the next game faster to build. Rockstar rejects the widely cited $1.5 billion budget figure.

items.title: First six radio stations revealed
items.summary: Rockstar previewed six in-game stations, including Flash FM, Cocoteo FM and Back Country Radio, plus on-demand podcasts.
items.body: Rockstar Games has previewed the first six radio stations of Grand Theft Auto VI, including Flash FM, Cocoteo FM and Back Country Radio. The game also gets on-demand podcasts, and radio and podcasts can be heard on foot with headphones too.

items.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream GTA VI at launch
items.summary: Xbox Cloud Gaming will stream GTA VI on consoles from day one. The deal is not exclusive and doesn't include PC.
items.body: The Verge reports that Xbox Cloud Gaming will stream Grand Theft Auto VI on consoles at launch. The story was later corrected: according to Xbox, the deal is not exclusive and streaming to PC is not included.
